scenarios.title: Forged/unsigned governed tap performs no payment and queues no write intent
scenarios.purpose: Prove an unauthenticated caller cannot cause a governed carrier-invoice effect: a Slack /slack/actions POST carrying a governed-approval-shaped token but no valid HMAC signature must be refused before any governed handling, leaving zero payment effect and zero queued write intent in the durable store.
scenarios.rationale: The whole feature's safety hinge is that only an authenticated, recorded approval can advance the pipeline; a forged tap is the single most likely real-world attack and must land nothing.
scenarios.requirement_reference: no payment effect occurs without a recorded approval

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous forged governed taps do not race into a double effect

scenarios.rationale: 'Paid exactly once' is a concurrency property; the classic failure is two near-simultaneous approvals both landing, so the race must be exercised, not assumed.

scenarios.title: Restart of the callback service fabricates no governed effect and leaves the audit store intact
scenarios.purpose: Restart the callback service, then send one forged governed tap, and confirm: the security_events store is still queryable (durable), zero governed writes were completed (restart did not fabricate an effect or auto-resume anything), and the service is still fail-closed after restart.
scenarios.rationale: A restart is where in-memory grant handles are deliberately dropped; the durable decision store must survive and the process must not resurrect or invent an effect on the way back up.
